Subject: ACME POC - Post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we can align on scope and timelines: 

1) Success criteria (what Acme will measure):
- Latency: 95th percentile < 500ms for single-turn classification calls
- Throughput: sustain 50 requests/min with batching enabled
- Accuracy: intents matched within 2% of current baseline on the evaluation set
- Stability: no more than 1% error rate over 72h test window

2) Evaluation plan:
- Week 1: Integration + smoke tests (internal team)
- Week 2: Run evaluation harness against 1k sample prompts you provide
- Week 3: Joint QA and performance tuning

3) Ownership:
- Redwood (technical lead): Mateo Alvarez — SDK + API integration, streaming setup, tool calling examples
- Acme (product/eng lead): Alex Tony — provide evaluation dataset, run trials, collate results

4) Integration requirements we discussed:
- Use Redwood JS SDK for quick start (example routes in attached checklist)
- API routes: /v1/generate for non-streaming, /v1/stream for server-streaming (SSE)
- Tool calling: we support structured tool calls (JSON schema) and a fallback text output; recommend explicit tool schemas for deterministic behavior

5) Timeline (proposed):
- Kickoff: Mon Nov 23
- Integration complete: Nov 27
- Evaluation run: Nov 30 - Dec 3

6) Deliverables:
- Redwood: sample SDK snippet, integration checklist, success criteria spreadsheet (attached)
- Acme: dataset (1k samples), test account credentials, sign-off on success criteria

Please confirm that the criteria look right and that the timeline works for your team. If so I’ll loop Mateo in to schedule a technical kickoff and share the integration checklist/attachments.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Alex / team —

Thanks Marissa — looping in with the technical details ahead of the kickoff. Attaching the checklist and including inline snippets and implementation notes below so your frontend/engineering leads can get a head start.

1) Quickstart (JS SDK)
- Install: npm i @redwood/inference
- Usage (non-streaming):
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-medium', route: '/v1/generate', input: prompt });

2) Streaming (SSE) example (client-side)
- Endpoint: POST /v1/stream
- Server sends events with prefix "event: token" for token-level updates
- Example: use EventSource for browser; we also have a Node helper in the SDK: client.stream({ model:'redwood-medium', input })

3) Tool calling / structured outputs
- We support JSON schema-driven tool calls. Example payload: {"tools": [{"name":"search","schema":{...}}], "input": "Find latest policy text"}
- If you need deterministic tool outputs, set call_mode: "strict" and provide tool validation rules; fallback will return plain text when validation fails

4) API routes & rate limits
- /v1/generate : sync responses, good for batch jobs
- /v1/stream : SSE for low-latency streaming responses
- /v1/embeddings : embedding vectors for similarity ops
- We'll start with a small rate limit for the trial (200rpm) and can increase for load tests

5) Auth & test accounts
- Use API key scoped to the trial project (we'll provision for acme-poc-123)
- For Private deployments we support VPC peering and API-level IP allowlists

6) Observability & metrics
- We can push token-level latency traces to your tracing endpoint and supply per-route dashboards in the Console.

Attached checklist includes end-to-end items (SDK install, sample calls, streaming test, tool-calling example, evaluation harness link). I’ll be on the kickoff and will own the integration work together with Dylan (cc’d) for infra and load testing.

Proposed time for kickoff (30m): Mon Nov 23, 11:00 AM PST — works for you?

Thanks,
Mateo
